items.text: Emergency disconnect outdoors, readily accessible, and marked as the emergency disconnect — not with a generic label.

Service disconnects (two to six): arranged per 230.71(B) — separate enclosures, panelboards with mains, barriered switchboard sections, or compartmented switchgear — and grouped as 230.71(A) requires.
Main bonding jumper present, sized per 250.28, and actually installed — verified by eye, not assumed from the factory strap.
Feeder to any subpanel: neutral isolated, ground bar bonded to the can, no bonding screw or strap left in a downstream panel.
One receptacle counted in EACH vehicle bay on the plan, not one per garage door remote location.
240V garage receptacle (welder, lift, compressor) checked for GFCI under the 2020 125–250V range in 210.8(A).
Dryer receptacle is 4-wire on new work, appliance bonding strap removed, and the circuit protected per S-08.
Detached structure fed from the house: its own disconnect at the building, its own electrodes, and a 4-wire feeder with isolated neutral.

Condenser on a 1- or 2-family dwelling: no GFCI required for listed and labeled HVAC equipment (FBC-R E3408.1 Exception No. 2 to 210.8(F)). Commercial or other outdoor outlets: confirm the 210.8(F) position with the AHJ and note it in the job file.
